Condo buildings in Mission BC
Briskham Manor — 7554 Briskham Street

Confirmed apartment-form. Built 1993 per most listings and the MLS data sheet (one listing says 1992 — the sheet/majority year, 1993, is used here and the conflict is noted). 33 units in the development, Strata Plan LMS1049 (MLS data sheet). Construction: frame wood with brick exterior and vinyl siding, 3 storeys. A well-managed 55+ complex; the MLS data sheet's bylaw fields record cats OK, dogs OK, a two-pet limit with restrictions, and current listings describe pets limited to roughly 24–25 lbs. Gas and hot water are included in the strata fees per listings, and parking is secure under-building. The sheet shows zoning MA1.
Mission Manor — 33165 2nd Avenue
Built 1992 (building directory, secondary source). The directory records restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
Glenkirk Court — 7436 Stave Lake Street

Built 1975, 38 units (MLS data sheet: units in development total 38, Strata Plan NW380, frame-wood construction, freehold strata). Listings note shared laundry, and one current listing states "No short term rentals" for the building. Any other restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Montgomery Condos — developer address 7375 Horne Street

(resale listings also address units at 33281 2 Avenue). Six storeys, 85 units, by Redekop Faye, with estimated completion in 2026 (developer source) — a presale/just-completed building, so REDMA applied to developer contracts. Current listings describe fall 2026 move-ins and note prices exclude GST with the First-Time Home Buyers' GST rebate available — both are new-build markers; verify the specific unit's status before relying on either.
Preston on Fourteenth ("The Preston") — 32690 14th Avenue

Built 2023 per current listings, by Redekop Faye. The presale record describes a 4-storey woodframe building of 103 condominiums plus 11 affordable rental units, and states condo rentals were permitted for 100 years under the project's housing agreement (presale source, secondary). Amenities in listings: clubhouse, exercise centre, yoga/games and co-working rooms, dog wash. Restrictions beyond the housing-agreement rental term: UNCONFIRMED.
Silver & Cedar — 8423 Cedar Street (Cedar Valley)
A six-storey woodframe building of 98 condominiums by Redekop Faye (presale-directory source, secondary). the building was completing as these notes were researched. Restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Ridgewood Place — 7265 Haig Street
Named in one current listing. Year built, unit count, construction and restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Stave Lake Landing — 33599 2nd Avenue

Built 1997 (building directory, secondary source). The directory records restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals not allowed — the rental line is void since November 24, 2022. The building's form (apartment vs townhome-style strata) was not fully settled from the directory snippet — form UNCONFIRMED; verify against the strata plan before counting it as apartment stock.

items.t: Board geography: Mission is a Fraser Valley board community with nine sub-areas — Dewdney Deroche, Durieu, Hatzic, Hemlock, Lake Errock, Mission, Mission West, Stave Falls and Steelhead. The core "Mission" sub-area holds most of the listings. Any rural fringe where the board's sub-area lines and the city boundary might differ is UNVERIFIED — no board street-level boundary is published.

Where the attached pool sits, September 2026 (inventory / solds / sales ratio, Condos & Townhomes): Mission 104 / 10 / 10%; Hemlock 9 / 0 / NA; Mission West 8 / 0 / NA; Lake Errock 1 / 0 / NA; all other sub-areas 0 / 0 / NA. The nine sub-area rows sum to the community totals in both splits.

Where the condo stock concentrates: the downtown/central core — 1st and 2nd Avenues, Horne Street, 7th Avenue and 14th Avenue (Montgomery, Mission Manor, Stave Lake Landing, Preston), the Cedar Street corridor in Cedar Valley (Silver & Cedar), and the Briskham Street pocket west of downtown (Briskham Manor, Briskham Hill).
SD75 runs elementary, middle and secondary tiers.

Transit — West Coast Express: TransLink's timetable effective January 5, 2026 runs five weekday trains westbound from Mission City Station at 5:25, 5:55, 6:25, 6:55 and 7:25 a.m., arriving Waterfront Station 75 minutes later, and five eastbound trains from Waterfront at 3:50, 4:20, 4:50, 5:30 and 6:20 p.m.; there is no service on weekends or statutory holidays. Mission City Station is at 33200 North Railway Avenue. BC Transit Route 31 runs Mission–Abbotsford.

Health care: Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, consists of a 25-bed medical inpatient unit, a 20-bed PATH unit and a 10-bed Christine Morrison Hospice, and provides primary acute care, outpatient and inpatient, general medicine, laboratory and diagnostic services; Fraser Health also lists a Mission Public Health Unit at 304 - 32555 London Ave.

items.t: Mission property tax penalty is a flat 10%: on current taxes left unpaid after the July 2 due date — the City's property tax page states a "10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding on July 3, 2026" (Community Charter ss. 233–234; Mission has no alternative-scheme bylaw). blocks.text: Good to know about Mission BC

items.t: Mission replaced its OCP in 2026. Bylaw 6405-2026 was adopted April 21, 2026, replacing Bylaw 6350-2025 — planning documents and listing copy citing the old OCP are already a bylaw out of date. The City states the new bylaw is substantively the same OCP, with a Regional Context Statement formally incorporated.

One developer is reshaping the city's condo map. Redekop Faye built Preston on Fourteenth (2023), Montgomery (completing 2026) and Silver & Cedar (completing 2026) — three of the city's newest apartment buildings share one builder, which makes cross-building comparisons of construction and warranty unusually direct.

Preston's rentals rest on a housing agreement, not just the 2022 law. Its presale record states condo rentals were permitted for 100 years — a project-level housing agreement term that survives independently of the province-wide voiding of rental bylaws.

Montgomery carries two addresses. The developer markets 7375 Horne Street while resale listings address units at 33281 2 Avenue — the same building. Confirm which address a specific unit's title and strata records use before ordering documents.

Luther Place also carries two addresses — 7525 Martin Place in listings, 32286 7th Avenue in the building directory — and its units surface in "condo" feeds even though the MLS dwelling type is Townhouse. Both facts will confuse a buyer's document search if not flagged up front.
The attached median is a small-sample number.
The core carries the market; the countryside barely registers attached.
A school name on a feed card is not a school.

Central amenities a condo buyer actually uses: Mission Leisure Centre at 7650 Grand Street and Mission Memorial Hospital at 7324 Hurd Street anchor the central core the condo buildings cluster around.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Mission BC

items.t: Form B diligence (the 4 cross-referenced strata complexes): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For Mission's oldest townhouse stock (Luther Place 1988, Cherry Lane 1989) this is the central diligence document.

Secondary suites (Mission's own rules — Surrey's figures are never carried in): all secondary suites in Mission must be registered with the City; a secondary suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; the registration period closed May 16, 2024, so adding a suite now goes through the building permit process, and an unregistered suite the City becomes aware of can be investigated and may require a decommission permit.

City property taxes — FLAT 10%: City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026. That is the whole penalty: a flat 10% on unpaid taxes after July 2 (Community Charter ss. 233–234 + Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s. 3; Mission has NO alternative-scheme bylaw under Charter s. 235). Keep the regimes separate: 5% after July 2 + a further 5% after October 31 is the separate RURAL regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11) for FVRD electoral areas outside the City — it is NOT the City penalty and is never blended here.

ALR (rural edges): Mission's rural sub-areas include farm land; on ALR parcels the ALC frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), and ALR residences cannot be stratified. Which parcels on this page's feed are in the ALR: UNVERIFIED — check parcel by parcel.

Flood and dykes: the Fraser River floodplain runs along the city's south edge and Hatzic Prairie sits behind the Dewdney Dyke system; Mission taxes also carry a diking levy. Flood status and insurance terms are parcel- and building-specific — check both.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Mission BC

items.t: OCP: City of Mission Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026 — ADOPTED APRIL 21, 2026 (standing correction): The research records the process in its own terms: Bylaw 6405-2026 was put to a public hearing on April 7, 2026 at City Hall, 8645 Stave Lake Street, to replace and repeal OCP Bylaw 6350-2025; the City states the new bylaw is substantively the same OCP — vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction unchanged — proposed to address a procedural matter and to formally incorporate a Regional Context Statement as required under the Local Government Act. Whether it had since been adopted was UNVERIFIED in the research pass; the standing correction above governs.

Zoning: City of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020: (cited in the City's own amending bylaws as "District of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020"). Parcel zone, minimum lot area and permitted uses are read from the consolidated bylaw per parcel; no city-wide lot-size table is documented in this research — UNVERIFIED as a table here.

SSMUH / added units (Mission frame): the City incorporated the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing legislation into Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020 on July 17, 2024 (Bylaw 6299-2024-5949(163)); as part of that amendment the Urban Residential 930 Secondary Dwelling Zone (R930s) was removed and merged with R930. Specific unit counts per lot size for Mission are UNCONFIRMED in this research — Surrey's 3/4/6-unit figures are NOT carried into Mission. Added-unit permission is not permission to subdivide.

Secondary suites (Mission's own rule): all secondary suites in Mission must be registered with the City; a suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; a new suite goes through the building permit process, and an unregistered suite can trigger a bylaw investigation and a possible decommission permit.

Development charges (context for a subdivision/build): the City's Development Cost Charge Bylaw 6348-2025 was adopted May 5, 2025, and DCCs apply to every person who obtains approval of a subdivision (among other triggers); the Amenity Cost Charge Bylaw 6349-2025 was adopted the same day, payable at subdivision approval or building permit issuance. Amounts are in the bylaws — none is quoted here.

ALR block (where ALR ground exists): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

Mission property taxes: due July 2, with a FLAT 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026 — Community Charter ss.233–234 + Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s.3; Mission has NO s.235 alternative-scheme bylaw. This is not Surrey's two-step 5% + 5%, and not the FVRD rural 5% + 5% regime.

Floodplain / hazard diligence: Parcel-level hazard, riparian and geotechnical items are read from the City's site-assessment process under DSCB 5650-2017 (Schedule J asks, among other things, about septic systems, ditching/ponds and vegetation) per application.

faq.q: What does the Mission community market look like overall?
faq.a: In September 2026, Mission recorded 231 detached listings with 28 solds at a $814,000 median (29 days on market), and 122 Condos & Townhomes listings with 10 solds at a $430,000 median (61 days) — community-level figures, which is the level this whole-city page covers (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which part of Mission holds most of the market?
faq.a: The core "Mission" sub-area: 170 of the community's 231 detached listings and 104 of its 122 attached listings in September 2026, and all 10 attached sales; the rural sub-areas (Hatzic, Hemlock, Lake Errock, Stave Falls, Steelhead, Durieu, Dewdney Deroche) are detached-led and low-count (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: How is the commute from Mission to downtown Vancouver?
faq.a: By West Coast Express: five weekday morning trains from Mission City Station (5:25–7:25 a.m.) reach Waterfront Station in 75 minutes, with five return trains in the afternoon (arriving Mission City 5:05–7:35 p.m.) and no weekend or holiday service, per TransLink's timetable effective January 5, 2026.

SD75 schools confirmed by name and address against the BC Ministry K-12 file include Mission Senior Secondary, Hatzic and École Heritage Park middle schools, and elementaries across the city from Mission Central and Windebank to Hatzic, Silverdale, Stave Falls, Dewdney and Deroche — the district runs elementary, middle and secondary tiers, and catchments are address-based, so confirm the exact address with the district (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/education/work/bc_k12_schools.csv, read 2026-11-01).

faq.q: When are Mission property taxes due, and what is the penalty?
faq.a: For 2026, City of Mission property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, and a 10% penalty was added to any current balances outstanding, including unclaimed home owner grants, on July 3, 2026.

faq.q: Is Cherry Lane a condo or a townhouse complex?
faq.a: Townhouse strata. The building directory's own product variants for Cherry Lane (32165 Seventh Avenue, built 1989, 22 units) include "Townhouse," and the same is true of Luther Place, whose MLS records state dwelling type Townhouse outright.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Mission condo?
faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, which is why the "rentals not allowed" directory lines for Cherry Lane and Stave Lake Landing are outdated law. Short-term rentals are different: a bylaw can still restrict them, and one current Glenkirk Court listing states "No short term rentals."

faq.q: What is the tax penalty if I miss Mission's July 2 deadline?
faq.a: A flat 10% penalty on any current balance outstanding on July 3, 2026 — not a staged 5% + 5%. The 5% + 5% pattern is the separate FVRD rural regime for electoral areas outside the City. Budget for the diking levy as an additional line on the Mission tax bill.

faq.q: How old is Mission's condo stock, really?
faq.a: It spans 1975 (Glenkirk Court) to 2026 completions (Montgomery, Silver & Cedar). The middle band — Mission Manor (1992) and Briskham Manor (1993) — is wood-frame, and Briskham's strata fee includes gas and hot water per listings, a real offset when comparing fees across eras.

faq.q: Do the new Redekop Faye buildings charge GST?
faq.a: Yes on developer sales — Montgomery and Silver & Cedar are new construction, so 5% GST applies, with the First-Time Home Buyers' GST rebate (up to $50,000 back on homes to $1 million) and the BC Newly Built Home Exemption (PTT fully exempt to $1.1 million) both in play for qualifying buyers. Preston (built 2023) is now resale stock, so a purchase there is generally GST-exempt.

faq.q: Where is Mission's actual townhouse stock?
faq.a: This city page cross-references them and adds none.

faq.q: Can I rent out my Mission townhouse?
faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, even where a directory still prints "rentals not allowed" (Cherry Lane, Luther Place). Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ townhouse in Mission?
faq.a: Yes — two of the four verified townhouse complexes are published as 55+: Cherry Lane and Luther Place. Andrew's Place (co-op) — different forms and tenures, in the 55-plus program. Confirm the registered 55+ bylaw on the Form B.
